text_mt: Duty is that beneficial purpose which has an injunction as its defining mark.
Now follows the examination of its cause [of valid knowledge].

sanskrit_iast: satsaṃprayoge puruṣasyendriyāṇāṃ buddhijanma tatpratyakṣam animittaṃ vidyamānopalambhanatvāt /
meaning: सत्संप्रयोगे पुरुषस्येन्द्रियाणां बुद्धिजन्म तत्प्रत्यक्षम् अनिमित्तं विद्यमानोपलम्भनत्वात् /
text_mt: When there is contact between a person's senses and what is present, the arising of awareness is direct perception; that is no cause [for knowing duty], because it apprehends only what is presently existent.

sanskrit_iast: autpattikas tu śabdasyārthena saṃbandhas tasya jñānam upadeśo 'vyatirekaś cārthe 'nupalabdhe tatpramāṇaṃ bādarāyaṇasyānapekṣatvāt /
meaning: औत्पत्तिकस् तु शब्दस्यार्थेन संबन्धस् तस्य ज्ञानम् उपदेशो ऽव्यतिरेकश् चार्थे ऽनुपलब्धे तत्प्रमाणं बादरायणस्यानपेक्षत्वात् /
text_mt: The relation between a word and its meaning is primordial, however; instruction is the means of knowing it, and it does not fail with respect to an unapprehended object; it is a means of valid cognition, according to Bādarāyaṇa, because of its independence [of other means].
Some maintain that it is an act [that is produced], because it is seen there [only upon effort].
And because of its simultaneity in different beings.
And because there is an increase of it with a multiplicity of agents.
The perception there, however, is equally [explicable on the view of manifestation].
The non-perception of that which exists is due to the non-arrival [of the sound] at the sensory realm.
It must be permanent, however, because its perception is for the sake of another [to convey meaning].
And because no connection [originating in time] is known.
If [words] were newly produced, they would convey nothing, because their meaning is not caused thereby.
The traditional transmission of those [words] already existent is for the sake of action, because their meaning is caused thereby.
In ordinary life, due to invariable restriction, there is contact in actual usage.
And some hold the Vedas to be recent [creations], because they bear the names of persons.
The priority of the word, however, has already been stated.
The other [names], however, are merely common phonetic resemblances.

sanskrit_iast: kṛte vā viniyogaḥ syāt karmaṇaḥ saṃbandhāt /
meaning: कृते वा विनियोगः स्यात् कर्मणः संबन्धात् /
text_mt: [An objection:] If it is something created, there could be subsidiary application, because of the connection of the action.

sanskrit_iast: āmnāyasya kriyārthatvād ānarthakyam atadarthānāṃ tasmād anityam ucyate /
meaning: आम्नायस्य क्रियार्थत्वाद् आनर्थक्यम् अतदर्थानां तस्माद् अनित्यम् उच्यते /
text_mt: [Objection:] Because traditional sacred text serves the purpose of action, those parts not serving that purpose are useless; therefore, [the Veda] is said to be non-eternal.

sanskrit_iast: vidhinā tv ekavākyatvāt stutyarthena vidhīnāṃ syuḥ /
meaning: विधिना त्व् एकवाक्यत्वात् स्तुत्यर्थेन विधीनां स्युः /
text_mt: However, forming a single unified statement with an injunctive rule, [such passages] serve the injunctive rules by way of corroborative commendation.

And the traditional authority [of both] is equal.

The objection is met: for contradiction would arise only in actual performance, but the verbal meaning is not itself part of the performance; therefore, it is tenable.

sanskrit_iast: āptā cānupapattiḥ prayoge hi virodhaḥ syāc chabdārthas tv aprayogabhūtas tasmād upapadyeta /
meaning: आप्ता चानुपपत्तिः प्रयोगे हि विरोधः स्याच् छब्दार्थस् त्व् अप्रयोगभूतस् तस्माद् उपपद्येत /

text_mt: And the seeing of the son is due to an error on the part of the performer.
The universality is relative to ritual eligibility.

sanskrit_iast: phalasya karmaniṣpattes teṣāṃ lokavatparimāṇataḥ phalaviśeṣaḥ syāt /
meaning: फलस्य कर्मनिष्पत्तेस् तेषां लोकवत्परिमाणतः फलविशेषः स्यात् /
text_mt: Since the fruit is brought about by the action, the difference in fruit among them must correspond to the measure [of performance], as in ordinary life.

sanskrit_iast: vidhir vā syād apūrvatvād vādamātrama hy anarthakam /
meaning: विधिर् वा स्याद् अपूर्वत्वाद् वादमात्रम ह्य् अनर्थकम् /
text_mt: [Objection:] It must rather be an injunctive rule, because [the passage conveys] something unprecedented; for a mere explanatory statement is purposeless.
Its status as a sentential complement has indeed been stated.

sanskrit_iast: vidhiś cānarthakaḥ kvacit tasmāt stutiḥ pratīyeta tatsāmānyād itareṣu tathātvam /
meaning: विधिश् चानर्थकः क्वचित् तस्मात् स्तुतिः प्रतीयेत तत्सामान्याद् इतरेषु तथात्वम् /
text_mt: And in some places an injunctive rule would be purposeless; therefore, eulogy is understood; and by resemblance to that, the same holds true in other cases.

sanskrit_iast: prakaraṇe sambhavannapakarṣo na kalpyeta vidhyānarthakyaṃ hi taṃ prati /
meaning: प्रकरणे सम्भवन्नपकर्षो न कल्प्येत विध्यानर्थक्यं हि तं प्रति /
text_mt: When syntactically possible in the context of the ritual topic, displacement [to another context] should not be assumed; for that would render the injunctive rule purposeless with respect to it.
And if it were an injunctive rule, there would be syntactic split.
[Objection:] Or it might be a reason, because of purposefulness and logical coherence.
Rather, it is commendation, because of its following the word [of injunction], and there is no injunction of it [independently].
If it is argued that eulogy of what is meaningless is improper—
Rather, it has a purpose because it is supplementary to an injunctive rule, just as in everyday life.

sanskrit_iast: yadi ca hetur avatiṣṭheta nirdeśāt sāmānyād iti ced avasthā vidhīnāṃ syāt /
meaning: यदि च हेतुर् अवतिष्ठेत निर्देशात् सामान्याद् इति चेद् अवस्था विधीनां स्यात् /
text_mt: And if the reason holds, [and] if it is argued that on account of generic mention [it applies everywhere], there would be instability of the injunctive rules.
Because of addressing inanimate things with meaning;
Because of connection with non-eternal things, mantras would be purposeless.
On the contrary, the sentential meaning is not distinct [from ordinary language];
The scriptural restatement serves to specify an attribute;
In a command, there is no blaming or finding fault with the action, because it is a preparatory purification;
It is a statement of teaching because there is no [prior] connection;
And the connection with non-eternal entities has already been explained;
And the teaching of indicative textual marks proves they possess meaning;
Because duty is rooted in verbal testimony, what is not based on verbal testimony should be disregarded.

sanskrit_iast: api vā kartṛsāmānyāt pramāṇam anumānaṃ syāt /
meaning: अपि वा कर्तृसामान्यात् प्रमाणम् अनुमानं स्यात् /
text_mt: Alternatively, because of the commonality of the agents, inference [of a lost Vedic text] constitutes a means of valid cognition.

sanskrit_iast: virodhe tv anapekṣyaṃ syād asati hy anumānam /
meaning: विरोधे त्व् अनपेक्ष्यं स्याद् असति ह्य् अनुमानम् /
text_mt: In case of conflict, however, it is to be disregarded, for inference holds only in the absence [of direct scriptural statement].
If it is argued that [a custom] is not contradictory when it does not disturb the orthodox instruction;
[We reply:] No, because the authority of scripture has a definitive measure.
Rather, when the cause is apprehended, the words used should be understood in that sense.

sanskrit_iast: teṣv adarśanād virodhasya samā vipratipattiḥ syāt /
meaning: तेष्व् अदर्शनाद् विरोधस्य समा विप्रतिपत्तिः स्यात् /
text_mt: Since conflict is not observed among them, there would be equal disagreement;
Or rather, [the usage] found in scripture [prevails], because it is the cause of that [understanding].
What is enjoined, however, should be understood through a means of valid cognition, because there is no contradiction.
If it is argued that it is a treatise on ritual performance;
And because the performance is everywhere, and because of the scripture on proximate position;
Because inference is restricted, that which is connected with it would be the means of valid cognition.

sanskrit_iast: api vā sarva dharmaḥ syāt tannyāyatvād vidhānasya /
meaning: अपि वा सर्व धर्मः स्यात् तन्न्यायत्वाद् विधानस्य /
text_mt: Rather, it belongs to all ritual duties, because the rule of injunction is based on that principle;
The subsidiary application occurs from textual occurrence;
And because there is no indicative textual mark of a permanent relation;
If it is objected that it would not apply in other regions;
[We reply:] It would apply, for the designation is relational, as in the case of 'one from Mathurā';
Or it is a duty of the rite, like sloping [ground];
Yet it is equivalent to a duty of the performer.
Because there is no scripture on the production of performance, there would be no restriction among words.
Because speech is produced by effort, it is susceptible to defect.
And having multiple words [for one meaning] is illogical.
In that case, correctness belongs [to the standard form] because of special cultivation;
And the other is due to incapacity, because of resemblance;
And because it is a single part, it would occur when there is an interchange of case-endings.
Because there is no injunction of application, the meaning is single, on account of non-division.
Rather, [the denotation of a word is] the generic form, because it serves ritual action.

sanskrit_iast: na kriyā syād iti cedarthāntare vidhānaṃ na dravyam iti cet /
meaning: न क्रिया स्याद् इति चेदर्थान्तरे विधानं न द्रव्यम् इति चेत् /
text_mt: If it is argued that there would be no action [with a generic form alone, and] if it is argued that the injunction pertains to another object and not to the individual substance;
[We reply:] Because [the individual] serves that purpose, the application is undivided.

sanskrit_iast: uktaṃ samāmnāyaidam arthyaṃ tasmāt sarvaṃ tadarthaṃ syāt /
meaning: उक्तं समाम्नायैदम् अर्थ्यं तस्मात् सर्वं तदर्थं स्यात् /
text_mt: The purpose of the Vedic revelation has been stated; therefore, everything [in it] must serve that purpose.

sanskrit_iast: api vā nāmadheyaṃ syād yadutpattāvapūrvam avidhāyakatvāt /
meaning: अपि वा नामधेयं स्याद् यदुत्पत्तावपूर्वम् अविधायकत्वात् /
text_mt: Or rather, [a word] should be a proper ritual designation when [the matter mentioned] in the origination [of the rite] is unexampled, because it is not injunctive [of an accessory].
When an accessory quality is taught, the connection is with the primary element.
And another scriptural injunction provides [that quality] as well.

sanskrit_iast: nāmadheye guṇaśruteḥ syād vidhānam iti cet /
meaning: नामधेये गुणश्रुतेः स्याद् विधानम् इति चेत् /
text_mt: If it be argued that in the proper ritual designation there is injunction because a quality is directly heard;
When there is a single word, it is like what serves another purpose.

sanskrit_iast: tadguṇās tu vidhāyer annavibhāgād vidhānārthe na ced anyena śiṣṭāḥ /
meaning: तद्गुणास् तु विधायेर् अन्नविभागाद् विधानार्थे न चेद् अन्येन शिष्टाः /
text_mt: However, those qualities would be enjoined if not taught by another [text], because there is no division in what serves to enjoin.
In the case of sacred grass and clarified butter, since the word is obtained without consecration, it does not denote that [consecration].
In the case of sprinkling-waters, [it is so] because of its connection with the functional purpose.
If it be argued that in the Vaiśvadeva rite there is an option;

sanskrit_iast: na vā prakaraṇāt pratyakṣavidhānāc ca na hi prakaraṇaṃ dravyasya /
meaning: न वा प्रकरणात् प्रत्यक्षविधानाच् च न हि प्रकरणं द्रव्यस्य /
text_mt: No, because of the context of the ritual topic and because of direct injunction; for the context of the ritual topic does not belong to a substance.
And mutual connection [between accessories] is devoid of purpose.
Words possessing prior [meanings] do not have the purpose of enjoining; that capacity belongs to the Vedic revelation.

sanskrit_iast: guṇasya tu vidhānārthe tadguṇāḥ prayoge syur anarthakā na hi taṃ pratyarthavattāsti /
meaning: गुणस्य तु विधानार्थे तद्गुणाः प्रयोगे स्युर् अनर्थका न हि तं प्रत्यर्थवत्तास्ति /
text_mt: If a quality were meant to be enjoined, its qualities would be purposeless in the performance; for there is no utility toward it.
Because there is no division in what serves to enjoin, they would be tenable as having the purpose of eulogy.

sanskrit_iast: ānarthakyād akāraṇaṃ kartur hi kāraṇāni guṇārtho hi vidhīyate /
meaning: आनर्थक्याद् अकारणं कर्तुर् हि कारणानि गुणार्थो हि विधीयते /
text_mt: No, because it is without purpose; instruments belong to the agent, for what serves an accessory is enjoined.
In doubtful cases, [the meaning is determined] from the remainder of the sentence.
Or from the beneficial purpose, because assumption [must apply to] only one part.

sanskrit_iast: bhāvārthāḥ karmaśabdās tebhyaḥ kriyā pratīyetaiṣa hy artho vidhīyate /
meaning: भावार्थाः कर्मशब्दास् तेभ्यः क्रिया प्रतीयेतैष ह्य् अर्थो विधीयते /
text_mt: Action words denote coming into being; from them an action is understood, for this is the object enjoined.
If it be argued that coming into being is the meaning of all [words];

sanskrit_iast: yeṣām utpattau sve prayoge rūpopalabdhis tāni nāmāni tasmāt tebhyaḥ parākāṅkṣā bhūtatvāt sve prayogai /
meaning: येषाम् उत्पत्तौ स्वे प्रयोगे रूपोपलब्धिस् तानि नामानि तस्मात् तेभ्यः पराकाङ्क्षा भूतत्वात् स्वे प्रयोगै /
text_mt: Those whose form is perceived in their own employment upon utterance are nouns; therefore, there is an expectation for another from them, because they are accomplished entities in their own employment.

sanskrit_iast: yeṣāṃ tūtpattāv arthe sve prayogo na vidyate tāny ākhyātāni tasmāt tebhyaḥ pratīyetāśritatvāt prayogasya /
meaning: येषां तूत्पत्ताव् अर्थे स्वे प्रयोगो न विद्यते तान्य् आख्यातानि तस्मात् तेभ्यः प्रतीयेताश्रितत्वात् प्रयोगस्य /
text_mt: On the other hand, those whose own employment upon utterance does not exist as an accomplished thing are verbs; therefore, it is understood from them, because performance is dependent [on them].
They are twofold: those that are secondary qualities and those that are primary elements.

sanskrit_iast: yair dravyaṃ na cikīrṣyate tāni pradhānabhūtāni dravyasya guṇabhūtatvāt /
meaning: यैर् द्रव्यं न चिकीर्ष्यते तानि प्रधानभूतानि द्रव्यस्य गुणभूतत्वात् /
text_mt: Those by which a substance is not intended to be affected are primary elements, because substance is secondary.

sanskrit_iast: yais tu dravyaṃ cikīrṣyate guṇas tatra pratīyeta tasya dravyapradhānatvāt /
meaning: यैस् तु द्रव्यं चिकीर्ष्यते गुणस् तत्र प्रतीयेत तस्य द्रव्यप्रधानत्वात् /
text_mt: However, those by which a substance is intended to be affected, a secondary quality is understood there, because it has substance as primary.

sanskrit_iast: dharmamātre tu karma syād anirvṛtteḥ prayājavat /
meaning: धर्ममात्रे तु कर्म स्याद् अनिर्वृत्तेः प्रयाजवत् /
text_mt: An action consisting merely of duty would be [primary], because of non-completion, like the fore-sacrifices.
Or, because of equal direct scriptural statement, it would share the nature of the others.

sanskrit_iast: na tadarthatvāl lokavat tasya ca śeṣabhūtatvāt /
meaning: न तदर्थत्वाल् लोकवत् तस्य च शेषभूतत्वात् /
text_mt: No, because it serves that purpose, as in ordinary life, and because it is subordinate.
In the case of the chanted hymn and recited laud, however, there is preparatory purification, like the offering-verse, because of denoting the recipient deity.

sanskrit_iast: arthena tv apakṛṣyeta devatānām acodanārthasya guṇabhūtatvāt /
meaning: अर्थेन त्व् अपकृष्येत देवतानाम् अचोदनार्थस्य गुणभूतत्वात् /
text_mt: It should be drawn away by the purpose, because recipient deities are not enjoined, and the purpose is a secondary quality.
Or, like the barren cow, it would serve a secondary quality.
and the quality would be purposeless;
and in the case of the barren cow, because of the inherence of purpose;
Or, because of having meaning, it would occur where it is stated.

sanskrit_iast: api vā śrutisaṃyogāt prakaraṇe stautiśaṃsatī kriyotpāttiṃ vidadhyātām /
meaning: अपि वा श्रुतिसंयोगात् प्रकरणे स्तौतिशंसती क्रियोत्पात्तिं विदध्याताम् /
text_mt: or rather, because of connection with direct scriptural statement, in the context of the ritual topic the verbs 'he chants' and 'he recites' enjoin the origination of an action;
and that expression would be purposeless;
and a different meaning is understood;
and designation is like ritual action;
the injunctive rule and the ritual verse have the same meaning because of the single word.

meaning: अपि वा प्रयोगसामर्थ्यान् मन्त्रो ऽभिधानवाची स्यात् /
text_mt: On the contrary, on account of its capacity in ritual performance, a mantra must be expressive of an assertion.
The name mantra applies to those [texts] that enjoin them.
Texts not traditionally recited are not mantras; for the division applies only to what is traditionally recited.
Among them, a ṛc is where the metrical foot is determined by the sense.
Or rather, a nigada should be a fourth [class], on account of a difference in ritual property.
Or rather, they are yajuses, because their nature is identical with that.
The difference in ritual property is due to a specific textual injunction.

sanskrit_iast: arthaikatvād ekaṃ vākyaṃ sākāṅkṣaṃ ced vibhāge syāt /
meaning: अर्थैकत्वाद् एकं वाक्यं साकाङ्क्षं चेद् विभागे स्यात् /
text_mt: On account of unity of meaning, [words constitute] a single sentence, if upon division they would require supplementation.
In the case of coordinate [independent clauses], there would be a syntactic split.
Elliptical extension completes the sentence, because it has equal application to all.
When there is a different verbal root, there is a distinct action, because an association has already been established.

sanskrit_iast: ekasyaivaṃ punaḥ śrutir aviśeṣād anarthakaṃ hi syāt /
meaning: एकस्यैवं पुनः श्रुतिर् अविशेषाद् अनर्थकं हि स्यात् /
text_mt: The reiteration of one and the same [action] in this manner would be purposeless, since there is no difference.
But [the statement] regarding the Full Moon is the context of the ritual topic, because no specific form is stated.

sanskrit_iast: viśeṣadarśanāc ca sarveṣāṃ sameṣu hy apravṛttiḥ syāt /
meaning: विशेषदर्शनाच् च सर्वेषां समेषु ह्य् अप्रवृत्तिः स्यात् /
text_mt: And because specific marks are seen; for if they were identical, there would be no distinct employment.
The subsidiary element, however, is due to connection with direct scriptural statement.

sanskrit_iast: codanā vā guṇānāṃ yugapacchāstrāc codite hi tadarthatvāt tasyatasyopadiśyeta /
meaning: चोदना वा गुणानां युगपच्छास्त्राच् चोदिते हि तदर्थत्वात् तस्यतस्योपदिश्येत /
text_mt: Or it is an injunction of subsidiary elements simultaneously taught by rule; for when enjoined, each would be prescribed for that purpose.
The Upāṃśuyāja should be like the Full Moon sacrifice.
The Āghāra and Agnihotra [are references to the complex of rites], because they lack specific offering matter.

sanskrit_iast: codanā vā śabdārthasya prayogabhūtatvāt tatsannidher guṇārthena punaḥ śrutiḥ /
meaning: चोदना वा शब्दार्थस्य प्रयोगभूतत्वात् तत्सन्निधेर् गुणार्थेन पुनः श्रुतिः /
text_mt: Or rather, it is an injunction, because the meaning of the word has become an actual performance; therefore its restatement in proximity is for the sake of the subsidiary quality.

sanskrit_iast: dravyasaṃyogāc codanā paśusomayoḥ prakaraṇe hy anarthako dravyasaṃyogo na hi tasya guṇārthena /
meaning: द्रव्यसंयोगाच् चोदना पशुसोमयोः प्रकरणे ह्य् अनर्थको द्रव्यसंयोगो न हि तस्य गुणार्थेन /
text_mt: In the case of the animal and Soma sacrifices, there is an injunction on account of connection with offering substances; for within the context of the ritual topic, a connection with an offering substance would be meaningless, since it is not for the sake of a subsidiary quality.

sanskrit_iast: tadbhedāt karmaṇo 'bhyāso dravyapṛthaktvād anarthakaṃ hi syād bhedo dravyaguṇībhāvāt /
meaning: तद्भेदात् कर्मणो ऽभ्यासो द्रव्यपृथक्त्वाद् अनर्थकं हि स्याद् भेदो द्रव्यगुणीभावात् /
text_mt: Repetition of the action is due to their difference; for due to the distinctness of the substance [the action] would be meaningless, [since] difference arises from the substance becoming subordinate.

sanskrit_iast: saṃskāras tu na bhidyeta parārthatvād dravyasya guṇabhūtatvāt /
meaning: संस्कारस् तु न भिद्येत परार्थत्वाद् द्रव्यस्य गुणभूतत्वात् /
text_mt: The preparatory purification, however, would not differ, because its purpose is external, since the offering substance is a subordinate factor.
And [difference arises from] a name, because of its connection with the origination [of the rite].
And it is a subsidiary qualification when there is connection with a transcendental potency, because the two sentences are equal.

sanskrit_iast: aguṇe tu karmaśabde guṇas tatra pratīyeta /
meaning: अगुणे तु कर्मशब्दे गुणस् तत्र प्रतीयेत /
text_mt: Where, however, the word denoting the action has no subsidiary quality, a subsidiary quality would be understood there.

sanskrit_iast: phalaśrutes tu karma syāt phalasya karmayogitvāt /
meaning: फलश्रुतेस् तु कर्म स्यात् फलस्य कर्मयोगित्वात् /
text_mt: Because of the direct scriptural statement of a result, however, it must be an independent action, since the result is connected with the action.

sanskrit_iast: atulyatvāt tu vākyayor guṇe tasya pratīyeta /
meaning: अतुल्यत्वात् तु वाक्ययोर् गुणे तस्य प्रतीयेत /
text_mt: Because of the inequality of the two sentences, however, [the result] would be understood as connected with the subsidiary quality.
When they are equal, it must be connected with the action.
In the case of the Saubhara chant, the connection with desire belongs to the finale, because of direct scriptural statement regarding the person.

sanskrit_iast: sarvasya voktakāmatvāt tasmin kāmaśrutiḥ syān nidhanārthā punaḥ śrutiḥ /
meaning: सर्वस्य वोक्तकामत्वात् तस्मिन् कामश्रुतिः स्यान् निधनार्था पुनः श्रुतिः /
text_mt: Or rather, because desire is stated for the whole, the direct statement of desire applies to that; the restatement is for the purpose of the finale.

sanskrit_iast: guṇas tu kratusaṃyogāt karmāntaraṃ prayojayet saṃyogasyāśeṣabhūtvāt /
meaning: गुणस् तु क्रतुसंयोगात् कर्मान्तरं प्रयोजयेत् संयोगस्याशेषभूत्वात् /
text_mt: A subsidiary quality, however, because of connection with the sacrificial rite, would instigate a distinct action, because the connection does not form a subordinate element.

sanskrit_iast: ekasya tu liṅgabhedāt prayojanārtham ucyetaikatvaṃ guṇavākyatvāt /
meaning: एकस्य तु लिङ्गभेदात् प्रयोजनार्थम् उच्येतैकत्वं गुणवाक्यत्वात् /
text_mt: In the case of one single [rite], however, difference of indicative marks is stated for a specific purpose; oneness [remains], because it is a sentence about a subsidiary quality.
In the Aveṣṭi rite, the primary sacrificial rite is spoken of, because of connection with sacrifice.
In the sacrificial courses, there is an independent injunction, because of the attachment of a name.
And the sentence is complete with respect to the result.
The attachment of the name is due to a subsidiary quality.
And it is a preparatory purification outside the context of the ritual topic, because there is no word expressing a ritual action.
Or [it extends] only so far as stated, because the rite is rooted in direct scriptural statement.
The root 'yaji' (to sacrifice), however, [denotes a distinct rite] on account of the connection with substance, fruit, and recipient, since these are connected with the rite.
That which is conjoined with an expressive term, however, has that purpose, because of its conjunction in direct scriptural statement.
In the pātnīvata cup, however, there is a limitation [of the offering] because of what precedes.
Agni, however, from the sight of the indicative textual mark, should be understood as the name of a sacrificial rite.
Or it may be a substance, because the injunctive rule has that as its object.

sanskrit_iast: tatsaṃyogāt kratus tadākhyaḥ syāt tena dharmavidhānāni /
meaning: तत्संयोगात् क्रतुस् तदाख्यः स्यात् तेन धर्मविधानानि /
text_mt: Because of connection with it, the sacrificial rite would bear that name; by that [interpretation] the prescriptions of details [are explained].
In a difference of context, there is a difference of purpose.
And [it denotes another rite when] a fruit [is mentioned] in the absence of proximity to the rite.

sanskrit_iast: saṃnidhau tv avibhāgāt phalārthena punaḥ śrutiḥ /
meaning: संनिधौ त्व् अविभागात् फलार्थेन पुनः श्रुतिः /
text_mt: In proximity, however, because there is no distinction, the repetition of the direct scriptural statement is for the sake of the fruit.
Because of being the cause of the Āgneya hymn, it would be understood as repetition.

sanskrit_iast: avibhāgāt tu karmaṇāṃ dvirukter na vidhīyate /
meaning: अविभागात् तु कर्मणां द्विरुक्तेर् न विधीयते /
text_mt: Because of the non-difference of the rites, however, [a distinct rite] is not enjoined by the reiteration.
Or the repetition of the direct scriptural statement serves another purpose.
The lifelong repetition is a property of the rite, on account of the context of the ritual topic.
Or [it is a property] of the agent, on account of the conjunction with direct scriptural statement.

sanskrit_iast: liṅgadarśanāc ca karmadharme hi prakrameṇa niyamyeta tatrānarthakam anyat syāt /
meaning: लिङ्गदर्शनाच् च कर्मधर्मे हि प्रक्रमेण नियम्येत तत्रानर्थकम् अन्यत् स्यात् /
text_mt: And on account of seeing an indicative textual mark; for if it were a property of the rite, it would be restricted by the initial performance, and then another [performance] would be meaningless.

sanskrit_iast: vyapavargaṃ ca darśayati kālaś cet karmabhedaḥ syāt /
meaning: व्यपवर्गं च दर्शयति कालश् चेत् कर्मभेदः स्यात् /
text_mt: And [the text] shows completion; if time [were the condition], there would be a difference of rites.
However, because of impermanence, this cannot be so.
And also there would be contradiction, as before.

sanskrit_iast: kartus tu dharmaniyamāt kālaśāstraṃ nimittaṃ syāt /
meaning: कर्तुस् तु धर्मनियमात् कालशास्त्रं निमित्तं स्यात् /
text_mt: Because of the restrictive rule of duty for the agent, however, the teaching regarding time would be an occasioning cause.

Because of the observation of names, forms, special details, repetition, censure, capacity, declaration of completion, expiation, and other reasons, there should be a difference of rites across different Vedic branches.
Or [the rite is] one, because there is no difference in connection, form, injunction, and name.
It cannot be [a difference] through name, because [such names] do not denote the injunction.
And all [branches] would have one single rite.
The teaching of ritual duty pertains to knowledge.
Or there is no repetition, because the conjunction with direct scriptural statement is non-different.
And it is not taught with reference to a single [person].
And the consideration is like that of completion.
Even when there is unity, the declarations of censure, capacity, and completion pertain to other [matters].
Expiation is on account of an occasioning cause.
Completion would be understood as already known, because of having a precedent.

sanskrit_iast: liṅgamaviśiṣṭaṃ sarvaśeṣatvān na hi tatra karmacodanā tasmāt dvādaśāhasyāhāravyapadeśaḥ syāt /
meaning: लिङ्गमविशिष्टं सर्वशेषत्वान् न हि तत्र कर्मचोदना तस्मात् द्वादशाहस्याहारव्यपदेशः स्यात् /
text_mt: The indicative textual mark is non-distinct because it is accessory to all; for there is no ritual injunction there; therefore, it would be a designation of the day-sequence of the twelve-day sacrifice.

sanskrit_iast: dravye cācoditatvād vidhīnām avyavasthā syān nirdeśād vyatiṣṭheta tasmān nityānuvādaḥ syāt /
meaning: द्रव्ये चाचोदितत्वाद् विधीनाम् अव्यवस्था स्यान् निर्देशाद् व्यतिष्ठेत तस्मान् नित्यानुवादः स्यात् /
text_mt: And because it is not enjoined with respect to substance, there would be no fixed determination of injunctive rules; [since] it is determined by designation, therefore it must be a constant restatement.
Because of the prohibition of what has been enjoined, in one alternative there would be an excess.
In the Sārasvata [sacrifice], because of conflict, the expression 'when' applies.
In the Upahavya, there is no counter-injunction.
Or the repeated scriptural statement is for the sake of a secondary quality.
And [scripture] also shows cognition.

sanskrit_iast: api vā kramasaṃyogād vidhipṛthaktvam ekasyāṃ vyavatiṣṭheta /
meaning: अपि वा क्रमसंयोगाद् विधिपृथक्त्वम् एकस्यां व्यवतिष्ठेत /
text_mt: Or, on account of connection with order, the diversity of injunctive rules would be restricted to one [branch].

sanskrit_iast: virodhinā tv asaṃyogād aikakarmye tatsaṃyogād vidhīnāṃ sarvakarmapratyayaḥ syāt /
meaning: विरोधिना त्व् असंयोगाद् ऐककर्म्ये तत्संयोगाद् विधीनां सर्वकर्मप्रत्ययः स्यात् /
text_mt: However, because there is no connection with anything contradictory, and because they are connected with that single ritual performance, the injunctive rules would produce cognition of the entire rite.
Bādari holds that it applies to substances, qualities, and preparatory purifications.
Jaimini holds that actions too [are accessory elements], because they are for the sake of the fruit.
And the fruit [is an accessory], because it is for the human purpose.
And the person [is an accessory], because he is for the sake of the rite.

sanskrit_iast: vihitas tu sarvadharmaḥ syāt saṃyogato 'viśeṣāt prakaraṇāviśeṣāc ca /
meaning: विहितस् तु सर्वधर्मः स्यात् संयोगतो ऽविशेषात् प्रकरणाविशेषाच् च /
text_mt: That which is enjoined, however, must be a property of all, because of non-distinction in connection and non-distinction in the context of the ritual topic.

sanskrit_iast: phalaṃ tu saha ceṣṭayā śabdārtho 'bhāvād viprayoge syāt /
meaning: फलं तु सह चेष्टया शब्दार्थो ऽभावाद् विप्रयोगे स्यात् /
text_mt: The fruit along with exertion, however, is the meaning of the word; for in separation it would result in non-existence.

sanskrit_iast: dravyaṃ cotpattisaṃyogāt tad artham eva codyeta /
meaning: द्रव्यं चोत्पत्तिसंयोगात् तद् अर्थम् एव चोद्येत /
text_mt: And substance, by virtue of its connection with origination, must be enjoined for that purpose alone.
When the purpose is one, there should be a restriction, because the substance and the quality serve a single action.
[The singular number] is attached to one [substance], because it is joined in the direct scriptural statement.

sanskrit_iast: sarveṣāṃ vā lakṣaṇatvād aviśiṣṭaṃ hi lakṣaṇam /
meaning: सर्वेषां वा लक्षणत्वाद् अविशिष्टं हि लक्षणम् /
text_mt: Or rather, [it applies] to all, because it serves as an indicator; for an indicator is indeterminate.
When it is enjoined [as a quality], however, it should be understood as directly stated by scripture, because it serves another purpose.
Or, on account of preparatory purification, there would be no fixed allocation of qualities.
Rather, there is a fixed allocation, because the purpose is connected by direct scriptural statement, and the word is the means of valid cognition for it.
[It applies] to its subsidiary elements, because otherwise there would be purposelessness.
With regard to a quality of the agent, however, there would be a syntactic split, because it does not inhere in the action.

sanskrit_iast: sākāṅkṣaṃ tv ekavākyaṃ syād asamāptaṃ hi pūrveṇa /
meaning: साकाङ्क्षं त्व् एकवाक्यं स्याद् असमाप्तं हि पूर्वेण /
text_mt: There must be a single unified statement when there is mutual syntactic requirement, for [the meaning] is incomplete with the prior alone.
Where there is doubt, however, there would be a syntactic split because of intervening separation.

sanskrit_iast: guṇānāṃ ca parārthattvād asambandhaḥ samatvāt syāt /
meaning: गुणानां च परार्थत्त्वाद् असम्बन्धः समत्वात् स्यात् /
text_mt: And because subsidiary qualifications exist for the sake of another, there would be no mutual connection between them, since they are equal.
And because mutually they have no connection of purpose.

sanskrit_iast: śeṣas tu guṇasaṃyuktaḥ sādhāraṇaḥ pratīyeta mithas teṣām asambandhāt /
meaning: शेषस् तु गुणसंयुक्तः साधारणः प्रतीयेत मिथस् तेषाम् असम्बन्धात् /
text_mt: The subsidiary element connected with a quality, however, should be understood as common [to all], because there is no mutual connection among them.

Or there is a fixed allocation, because of connection with the purpose; because the indicative textual mark is connected with the purpose, the direct scriptural mention of the quality serves as an indicator.

sanskrit_iast: arthābhidhānasāmarthyān mantreṣu śeṣabhāvaḥ syāt tasmād utpattisambandho 'rthena nityasaṃyogāt /
meaning: अर्थाभिधानसामर्थ्यान् मन्त्रेषु शेषभावः स्यात् तस्माद् उत्पत्तिसम्बन्धो ऽर्थेन नित्यसंयोगात् /
text_mt: The subsidiary status in the case of Vedic recitations is due to their capacity to express the meaning; therefore, their original connection is with that purpose, because of their constant association.
Because it is purificatory, it would apply even to what is not enjoined.
However, by virtue of direct statement, the Aindrī verse would apply contrary to its primary meaning.
Or rather, the designation is figurative, because the relation is not caused by the scriptural text.
No, it is an injunction of time, because [the action itself] has been enjoined elsewhere;
And there would be a frustration of the injunctive rule if it were a direct primary instruction.
Likewise with rising up and discharging.
And in the sūktavāka formula, it is an injunction of time, because it serves another purpose.
Or it is a direct primary instruction, for the word yājyā is not without reason.
It is accompanied by the purpose of the deity, because of its connection with it.
If it is objected that it is a disposal rite, [we reply that] like the sviṣṭakṛt offering, it would be a dual consecration.
Because there is instruction of the whole, the word 'all' applies to both.
Or [it applies] according to the purpose, because it is a preparatory purification of what has become subsidiary remainder.
[We reply:] Because there is no division in the ritual topic, the word 'whole' applies to both.
On account of the indicative textual mark, sequence, and contextual nomenclature, the traditional recitation is connected with the optional rite.
And in the primary eligibility, the Vedic recitation is enjoined, because it is instructed among rites not bearing that name.
Or it belongs to the rite bearing that name, because of the context of the ritual topic and appropriateness.

sanskrit_iast: anarthakaś copadeśaḥ syād asambandhāt phalavatā na hy upasthānaṃ phalavat /
meaning: अनर्थकश् चोपदेशः स्याद् असम्बन्धात् फलवता न ह्य् उपस्थानं फलवत् /
text_mt: And the instruction would be purposeless, because of the lack of connection with what has a fruit; for attending upon [the fire] produces no fruit.
And because [the hymns] are instructed for all.
By indicative textual mark and contextual nomenclature, the anuvāka section serves the purpose of consumption.
From its characteristic form and instructions, there is setting aside, because the purpose has already been enjoined.

sanskrit_iast: guṇābhidhānān mandrādir ekamantraḥ syāt tayor ekārthasaṃyogāt /
meaning: गुणाभिधानान् मन्द्रादिर् एकमन्त्रः स्यात् तयोर् एकार्थसंयोगात् /
text_mt: On account of the mention of the quality, 'mandrā' and the rest constitute a single Vedic recitation, because the two are connected with a single purpose.
Because of the specific designation of the indicative textual mark, non-Indra cups are devoid of the Vedic recitation among those of similar rule.
Or [it is recited] according to the deity, for the text shows that as the archetypal model.
In the case of re-drawn cups, there is mention of all, because there is no distinction.
Or, on account of removal, there is no mention of the former;
Or the removal is effected by the drawing [of the new portion].
Or it would be removed by the drawing.
One should, however, mention Tvaṣṭṛ, on account of his drinking.
Because they are not equal, however, it would not be so.
And the thirty [gods are not mentioned], because they serve another purpose.
And the vaṣaṭ-utterance is treated like the agent.
The exclusion of the metre, however, applies to all, because it is universally applicable.
In the Aindrāgna cup, however, [neither metre is mentioned], because the indicative textual mark is absent.
Or [one is mentioned] in one case, as in the division concerning another deity.
Or [the mention applies] to all, because of the absence of a cup possessing only a single metre.

sanskrit_iast: sarveṣāṃ vaikamantryam aitiśāyanasya bhaktipānatvāt savanādhikāro hi /
meaning: सर्वेषां वैकमन्त्र्यम् ऐतिशायनस्य भक्तिपानत्वात् सवनाधिकारो हि /
text_mt: Or, according to Aitiśāyana, all have a single Vedic recitation, because drinking is figurative; for the entitlement belongs to the soma-pressing.
By direct scriptural statement, the entitlement would belong to the caste.

sanskrit_iast: dharmopadeśāc ca na hi dravyeṇa sambandhaḥ /
meaning: धर्मोपदेशाच् च न हि द्रव्येण सम्बन्धः /
text_mt: And because [such qualities] are taught as properties [of the Veda]; for there is no direct connection with the substance.
And because of the designation 'threefold knowledge' (trayīvidyā); for one knowing it is designated accordingly.
If it be argued that in the case of a conflict of particular [Vedas], the rule should be according to the direct text;
Because of connection with the Veda, it would not be set aside by the context of the ritual topic.
In a conflict between a secondary and a principal element, the connection with the Veda belongs to the principal, because [the secondary] exists for the sake of that.
Where both are directly mentioned, [it belongs to that which has] predominance.
What is unconnected [with a particular Veda is determined] by the context of the ritual topic, because of the need for modal procedure.
And [it is determined by] relative textual position, from the identity of place.

When direct scriptural statement, indicative textual mark, syntactic unity, context of the ritual topic, relative textual position, and contextual nomenclature occur together, each later one is weaker, because of the remoteness of the sense.
[The mention of] the multi-day sacrifice is secondary, because of the context of the ritual topic.
But because there is no connection with the principal rite, it must be detached from it.
Or rather, [the auxiliary] is linked with duality or plurality, because of its injunctive rule.
If it be argued that it belongs as an alternative to that which has accomplished its purpose;
And the tail-end offering (jāghanī) [is taken from the animal victim], because it is a part of it.
That is not so; because it is accomplished without scriptural prescription from the archetypal sacrifice.
The joining together [of the sacrificial post] would belong to the archetypal sacrifice, like the purchase [of soma], because nothing would be rendered useless.
Or rather, there is transposition [to another rite], because of the mention of a specific characteristic.
Or it is determined by the performer, because the specific characteristic is occasioned by him.
Or it is determined by the sacrificial rite, because the corroborative statement would not otherwise be possible.
And [it applies to all] completion forms, like the performer, because the purpose of holding is undistinguished.
Or rather, [it applies] to the Ukthya and subsequent forms, because the object exists there.
If it be argued that, without distinction, the eulogy would be meaningless;
What is connected with a number would belong to the sacrificial rite, on account of the context of the ritual topic.
Or it is occasional, due to the connection with the performer, because the indicative mark is occasioned by him.
The grinding [of the oblation] for Pūṣan should be understood in the ectypal sacrifice, because it is not enjoined in the archetypal sacrifice.
[It would apply] to all its [oblations], because there is no distinction.

meaning: चरौवार्थोक्तं पुरोडाशे ऽर्थविप्रतिषेधात् पशौ न स्यात् /
text_mt: Or it is stated with purpose only in the boiled rice offering [and] in the sacrificial cake, because there would be a conflict of purpose in the animal victim, so it cannot be there.
And because there is no conflict of properties.
Or rather, it could occur where there is a second deity, because it is occasioned by the deity.

sanskrit_iast: vacanāt sarvapeṣaṇaṃ taṃ prati śāstravatvād arthābhāvād vicarāv apeṣaṇaṃ bhavati /
meaning: वचनात् सर्वपेषणं तं प्रति शास्त्रवत्वाद् अर्थाभावाद् विचराव् अपेषणं भवति /
text_mt: By explicit statement, there is grinding of the whole, since the scripture applies to that; while there is no grinding in the boiled rice offering, because the purpose is absent.

sanskrit_iast: ekasmin vārthadharmatvād aindrāgnav adubhayor na syād acoditatvāt /
meaning: एकस्मिन् वार्थधर्मत्वाद् ऐन्द्राग्नव् अदुभयोर् न स्याद् अचोदितत्वात् /
text_mt: Or rather, [grinding occurs] in the single [oblation to Pūṣan], because it is a property of the substance; it could not occur in both [deities], as in the offering to Indra and Agni, because it is not enjoined.
Being toothless is merely the reason.
[The rule] 'wearing the upper cloth suspended around the neck' is a human property, because the word makes that primary.
Or it is a reference [to something else], because the purpose is already established.
It should be an injunctive rule, because it conveys something previously unknown.
From general prevalence, it must be a property of the ritual action.
In its context, that which is connected with it [applies to it], because there is no contradiction.

sanskrit_iast: tatpradhāne vā tulyavat prasaṃkhyānād itarasya tadarthatvāt /
meaning: तत्प्रधाने वा तुल्यवत् प्रसंख्यानाद् इतरस्य तदर्थत्वात् /
text_mt: Or [it belongs] to that which is primary, because it is enumerated equally, while the other serves its purpose.
Or it is a corroborative statement, because of the context of the ritual topic.
And because it forms a single unified statement with the injunctive rule.
And the division of directions is likewise, because the connection is the cause of the purpose.
And [the statements regarding what is cut] at the joint, full, clarified butter, and burnt are likewise.
A non-action connected with the sacrificial rite would be a permanent restatement, because of the connection.
Or it is an injunctive rule, because of a distinct connection.
Like the multi-day sacrifice, it belongs to the person, because it serves his purpose.
Or, because of the specific context of the ritual topic, it is a preparatory purification of that which is connected with it, like a substance.
Because of specific designation, it must be detached.
And because at the Śaṃyu [recitation] there is an offering of everything.
Because before that there is exclusion of the woman in her stained garment.
Outside the context of the ritual topic, however, its attributes [apply universally], because there is no particular distinction.
Since there is no sacrificial substance, however, it must be an accessory element.

sanskrit_iast: syād vāsya saṃyogavat phalena sambandhas tasmāt karmaitiśāyanaḥ /
meaning: स्याद् वास्य संयोगवत् फलेन सम्बन्धस् तस्मात् कर्मैतिशायनः /
text_mt: Or rather, like a connection, it has an association with the fruit; therefore it is an independent act, so holds Aitiśāyana.
Subsidiaries [apply] in the context of the ritual topic without distinction to all actions.
The oblations, however, would be restricted [to the Āhavanīya], because of connection with the Āhavanīya.

sanskrit_iast: doṣāt tv iṣṭir laukike syāc chāstrād dhi vaidika na doṣaḥ syāt /
meaning: दोषात् त्व् इष्टिर् लौकिके स्याच् छास्त्राद् धि वैदिक न दोषः स्यात् /
text_mt: Because of a fault, however, the sacrifice would be in the worldly [sphere]; for according to scripture, in the Vedic [sphere] there would be no fault.
Or it is an explanatory praise, because [otherwise the fault] would be inexplicable; therefore it is to be understood in the sacrifice.
And it is not enjoined [for worldly acts], because of the difference of actions.

sanskrit_iast: doṣāt tu vaidike syād arthād dhi laukike na doṣaḥ syāt /
meaning: दोषात् तु वैदिके स्याद् अर्थाद् धि लौकिके न दोषः स्यात् /
text_mt: Because of a fault, however, it must be in the Vedic [sphere]; for from practical purpose there would be no fault in the worldly [sphere].
Or [it belongs to] the master [sacrificer], because it serves his purpose.
There is offering of the entire sacrificial substance, because it serves that purpose.
From cutting off portions, however, there would be a remainder.

sanskrit_iast: kṛtatvāt tu karmaṇaḥ sakṛt syād dravyasya guṇabhūtatvāt /
meaning: कृतत्वात् तु कर्मणः सकृत् स्याद् द्रव्यस्य गुणभूतत्वात् /
text_mt: Because the action is accomplished, however, it should occur once, since the substance is subordinate.
Because they do not prompt [the main rite], they should be performed from one [substance], since the remainder is subordinate.
Or from all, because there is no difference in cause, since preparatory purification serves that purpose.
If from one, [it may be] as desired, because there is no distinction.
Or from the principal one, because of prior sequence.
Since consumption is not heard, the word 'gift' denotes hiring.
Or it serves the purpose of consumption, because it is identical in substance.
Because of special assignment, there is commendation of the gift.
And from clarified butter, because of connection with all.
And in the case of clarified butter, because the Sviṣṭakṛt oblation is seen as serving that purpose.

sanskrit_iast: aśeṣatvāt tu naivaṃ syāt sarvādānād aśeṣatā /
meaning: अशेषत्वात् तु नैवं स्यात् सर्वादानाद् अशेषता /
text_mt: Because there is no remainder, however, it would not be so; there is no remainder due to taking all.
Because of commonality, it would not be in the dhruvā ladle.

sanskrit_iast: avattatvāc ca juhvāṃ tasya ca homasaṃyogāt /
meaning: अवत्तत्वाच् च जुह्वां तस्य च होमसंयोगात् /
text_mt: And because it is portioned into the juhū ladle, and that is connected with the oblation.
No, because of conflict with the injunction, and because it is the design of the sacrificial oblation.
Because the ritual title has arisen, the word 'all' applies when [a remainder] exists.
In the Sākamprasthāyya rite, the Sviṣṭakṛt and the iḍā are likewise.
And in the Sautrāmaṇī, regarding the cups.
Though the substance is one, they should be performed per action, because of the difference of actions.
And because the remainder is undivided, since it is non-distinct in relation to all.

sanskrit_iast: aindravāyave tu vacanāt pratikarma bhakṣaḥ syāt /
meaning: ऐन्द्रवायवे तु वचनात् प्रतिकर्म भक्षः स्यात् /
text_mt: With regard to the Aindravāyava cup, however, consumption must occur per action, because of direct statement.
In the case of Soma, because there is no direct statement, consumption does not exist.
Or it should exist, because another purpose is seen.

sanskrit_iast: vacanāni tv apūrvatvāt tasmād yathopadeśaṃ syuḥ /
meaning: वचनानि त्व् अपूर्वत्वात् तस्माद् यथोपदेशं स्युः /
text_mt: The direct statements, however, [are authoritative] because they are unprecedented; therefore they should follow the instruction.
In the case of the goblets, [consumption is determined] from contextual nomenclature, because the connection is caused by that.
One [drinks] from the Udgātṛ's goblet, because of direct scriptural statement.
Or all [drink], because of connection with all.
Or [the cup belongs] to the singers of the stotra, because of their connection with it, since there is a plural direct scriptural statement.

sanskrit_iast: sarve tu vedasaṃyogāt kāraṇād ekadeśe syāt /
meaning: सर्वे तु वेदसंयोगात् कारणाद् एकदेशे स्यात् /
text_mt: All [the chanter-priests partake], however, because of their connection with the Veda; [partaking] would apply to a single part because of an assigned cause.
For the grāvastut priest, no drinking [of Soma] is found, because of the absence of textual mention.
Or [he does partake] at the hāriyojana offering, because of connection with all.
Or [it is shared] among the cup-holders, because of proximity.
All [officiating priests partake], however, because it is an injunctive rule; the direct scriptural mention of the cup-holder is for that purpose.
And one should partake because of pronouncing the vaṣaṭ-call,
Because of direct teaching regarding the cups, [the partaker] is unspecified in the case of the remainder [of the havis].

sanskrit_iast: syād vā kāraṇabhāvād anirdeśaś camasānāṃ kartus tadvacanatvāt /
meaning: स्याद् वा कारणभावाद् अनिर्देशश् चमसानां कर्तुस् तद्वचनत्वात् /
text_mt: Or rather, because of the presence of a cause, the non-specification of the cups [means they belong to the agent], because the word denotes the agent.
When there is a single vessel, the adhvaryu should partake first, in order.
Because of express statement, partaking takes place only when permitted.
He should request permission with the formula 'Invited, invite!', because of textual suggestion.
There, the response follows from purpose.
When removed by the removal of the offering-verse, the partaking is removed, as in the case of the pravara invocation.
Because it has commenced, the pravara invocation is not set aside.
The fruit-cup is an occasional modification of the drink, because of direct scriptural connection.
Or [it is] a modification of the oblation, because the preparatory purification serves that purpose,
and because it is contemporary with the cups,
Among those who crawl behind, [partaking is shared] because of commonality.
Or it applies to the Brāhmaṇas, because of equality of the word.
It applies to all, because it is not within a specific context of the ritual topic.
Or [it applies] in the archetypal sacrifice, because there is no repetition.
Except that [it applies] when it has arrived through express statement.
Because of the completeness of the injunctive purpose, however, it serves the archetypal sacrifice, since conflict with the principal rite is precluded.
Because of a distinction of context of the ritual topic, however, it would conflict in an ectypal sacrifice.
An occasional rite, however, is a modification thereof in the archetypal sacrifice, because of a specific connection.
The setting up of the sacred fires is for the sake of the iṣṭi sacrifices, because of the context of the ritual topic.
Or rather not, because those [iṣṭis] are for the sake of that [setting up of fires],
It serves the archetypal sacrifice, just like other non-contextual statements.
Or it serves all purposes, because the establishment of the sacred fires has its own time.
[If] the fire for those [iṣṭis] were to come from the archetypal sacrifice, it would be like the fore-offerings.
Or rather not, because they are for the sake of that [fire].
The animal-sacrifice rule is identical for all, because there is no difference in the context of the ritual topic.

sanskrit_iast: śvas tv ekeṣāṃ tatra prākśrutir guṇārthā /
meaning: श्वस् त्व् एकेषां तत्र प्राक्श्रुतिर् गुणार्था /
text_mt: In the view of some, however, [it takes place] on the morrow; in that case, the earlier direct scriptural statement serves a subsidiary quality.
If it be said that thereby it is an injunctive rule of time for what has been deferred,
no, because of contradiction with direct scriptural statement.
Because of relative textual position, however, the earlier preparatory purification serves that purpose,
Because of the difference of time of the two milkings, the boiled milk would be disconnected.
Or, because of the division of the context of the ritual topic, the teaching of time applies to that which is connected with it.
Similarly, the textual mention of the cup is in another extraction-session.
And the girdle [is used], because of indicative textual marks.
[An item] taught remotely [and] not connected [with a specific rite belongs to that rite] due to proximity to the others.
Or rather, it is connected [with the principal rite], because it is for its sake, since the subsidiary element is occasioned by that.
By virtue of specific mention, it would be restricted.
Likewise, a subsidiary element of the fire [taught] outside a ritual context [applies everywhere].
An occasional rite, because it is not equal, would not have the same rule.
likewise, because of the singularity of purpose.
And because [a substitute] is not defined by scripture.
The direct scriptural statement of a secondary quality is for the purpose of restrictive injunction.
The terminal forms, however, share the same procedure, because of the non-difference of the ritual context.
And the designation applies equally.
There is modification, however, in connection with an optional desire, while the obligatory [form remains] the same.
Or rather, because of being stated twice, they will belong to the archetypal sacrifice.
And because of the negative prohibition of the earlier indicative marks.
The designation of one is on account of a particular qualification.
Owing to the specificity of the ritual context, what is unconnected belongs to the principal rite.
Or it belongs to all, because being subsidiary is not prompted by that alone.
no, for that sentence serves that purpose.
However, because of connection with the result, what is connected with the owner belongs to the principal rite.

sanskrit_iast: tadyukte tu phalaśrutis tasmāt sarvacikīrṣā syāt /
meaning: तद्युक्ते तु फलश्रुतिस् तस्मात् सर्वचिकीर्षा स्यात् /
text_mt: When connected with that, however, there is direct scriptural statement of the result; therefore there would be desire to perform everything.
Because of the designation of a secondary quality, the designation is for the sake of all.
The initiation and the sacrificial fee, however, belong to the principal rite by textual declaration.
Or it is merely [the designation of] a place, because of syntactical integration with what is taught.

sanskrit_iast: sāmadhenīs tad anvāhur iti havir ddhānayor vacanāt sāmadhenīnām /
meaning: सामधेनीस् तद् अन्वाहुर् इति हविर् द्धानयोर् वचनात् सामधेनीनाम् /
text_mt: Because of the declaration, 'They recite the kindle-verses following that', in regard to the two cart-sheds, [the place is] of the kindle-verses.

sanskrit_iast: deśamātraṃ vā pratyakṣaṃ hy arthakarma somasya /
meaning: देशमात्रं वा प्रत्यक्षं ह्य् अर्थकर्म सोमस्य /
text_mt: Or it is merely a place, for the primary functional action of the Soma is directly perceived.

sanskrit_iast: śāstraphalaṃ prayoktari tallakṣaṇatvāt tasmāt svayaṃ prayoge syāt /
meaning: शास्त्रफलं प्रयोक्तरि तल्लक्षणत्वात् तस्मात् स्वयं प्रयोगे स्यात् /
text_mt: The fruit taught by scripture accrues to the user, because of being characterized by him; therefore it should be in his own performance.

sanskrit_iast: utsarge tu pradhānatvāc cheṣakārī pradhānasya tasmād anyaḥ svayaṃ vā syāt /
meaning: उत्सर्गे तु प्रधानत्वाच् छेषकारी प्रधानस्य तस्माद् अन्यः स्वयं वा स्यात् /
text_mt: In abandoning, however, because of being the principal, the performer of subsidiary elements belongs to the principal; therefore another, or [he] himself, would be [the performer].

sanskrit_iast: anyo vā syāt parikrayāmnānād vipratiṣedhāt pratyag ātmani /
meaning: अन्यो वा स्यात् परिक्रयाम्नानाद् विप्रतिषेधात् प्रत्यग् आत्मनि /
text_mt: Or it must be another, because hiring is recorded, and because of contradiction in oneself.
There, the measure of performers would be from the purpose; there is no restriction, because of non-distinction.

sanskrit_iast: api vā śruti bhedāt pratināmadheyaṃ syuḥ /
meaning: अपि वा श्रुति भेदात् प्रतिनामधेयं स्युः /
text_mt: Or rather, because of the distinction of direct scriptural statements, they should be according to each proper designation.
If it be said that it is of one person through diversity of actions,
And the Camasādhvaryus [are distinct], because of designation by them.
At the origin, however, because of direct scriptural mention of plurality,
[there is] a ten-fold number, because an indicative textual mark is seen.
Or [he is one of the priests] on account of the ritual context, because of non-connection with an originative injunction.
And the sub-singers [are distinct], because an indicative textual mark is seen.
The seller, however, is another [person], because his action is not enjoined.
Because of performing actions, the status of officiating priest would belong to all, without distinction.
The restriction, however, is by the sacrificial fees, because of connection with direct scriptural statement.
And having stated the status of sacrificer, because initiation is enjoined for them [in the sacrificial session].
They are seventeen including the master, on account of the commonality of action.

sanskrit_iast: te sarvārthāḥ prayuktatvād agnayaś ca svakālatvāt /
meaning: ते सर्वार्थाः प्रयुक्तत्वाद् अग्नयश् च स्वकालत्वात् /
text_mt: They serve all purposes, because they are employed [for the whole], and the fires [serve all], because of their own time.
Because of connection with that, there would be restriction of the action, since the connection has a beneficial purpose.
Its specification is through instruction and contextual nomenclature.
And like that is the indicative textual mark seen.
The reciting of direction belongs to the Maitrāvaruṇa, on account of instruction.
Or the entitlement to the introductory verse [belongs to him], because of proximity to the direction.
And in the morning recitation (prātar-anuvāka), because the Hotṛ is seen [to be the performer].
The cup-adhvaryus (camasādhvaryus) [should perform the duties concerning] the cups, on account of the contextual nomenclature (samākhyā).
Or rather the Adhvaryu [performs them], because that is the general rule.
Due to instruction in the Veda, as before, when the Veda is different, they should be according to instruction.

sanskrit_iast: tadguṇād vā svadharmaḥ syād adhikārasāmathyāt sahāṅgair avyaktaḥ śeṣe /
meaning: तद्गुणाद् वा स्वधर्मः स्याद् अधिकारसामथ्यात् सहाङ्गैर् अव्यक्तः शेषे /
text_mt: Or, because of being mentioned there, it would have its own duty, by virtue of the capacity of ritual eligibility, along with its subsidiary elements; in the remainder, it is unmanifest.
The hiring is the master's action, because the action is for his sake.
Preparatory purifications, however, regarding human capacity, would be distributed according to the Veda, just like the actions.
Those pertaining to the sacrificer (yājamāna), however, [are his], because he is principal, just like the action.
Because of not being equal, they would not have identical rules.
Austerity also [belongs to the sacrificer], because of the accomplishment of the fruit, as in worldly affairs.

sanskrit_iast: guṇatvāc ca vedena na vyavasthā syāt /
meaning: गुणत्वाच् च वेदेन न व्यवस्था स्यात् /
text_mt: And because of being secondary, there would be no strict distribution according to the Veda.
Likewise desire, because of connection with the purpose.
It would belong to the others because of designation.
And mantras that do not effect an action are likewise.
When [a mantra is] handed down twice, both [priests use it], because the twofold tradition has beneficial purpose.

sanskrit_iast: jñāte ca vācanaṃ na hy avidvān vihito 'sti /
meaning: ज्ञाते च वाचनं न ह्य् अविद्वान् विहितो ऽस्ति /
text_mt: And causing to recite [takes place] when it is known; for an ignorant person is not enjoined.
The rites [belong] to the sacrificer because of the designation 'belonging to the sacrificer' (yājamāna).

sanskrit_iast: adhvaryur vā tadartho hi nyāyapūrve samākhyānam /
meaning: अध्वर्युर् वा तदर्थो हि न्यायपूर्वे समाख्यानम् /
text_mt: Or it is the Adhvaryu priest, for he is intended for that; indeed, the contextual nomenclature is preceded by logical principle.

sanskrit_iast: vipratiṣedhe karaṇaḥ samāvāyaviśeṣād itaram anyas teṣāṃ yato viśeṣaḥ syāt /
meaning: विप्रतिषेधे करणः समावायविशेषाद् इतरम् अन्यस् तेषां यतो विशेषः स्यात् /
text_mt: In case of conflict, the instrument [determines it], from the distinction of association; another [performs] the other, whence their distinction would arise.
Or [the term 'adhvaryu'] is figurative, because of commonality of action.
The fruit [belongs] to the officiating priest in the case of instruments, because of being meant for that.
Or rather to the master (yajamāna), because [the rite] is for his sake.
The fruit, however, belongs to their actions, because it has purpose with respect to the master [of the sacrifice].
The preparatory purification of substance belongs to all actions, because there is no distinction in the context of the ritual topic.
However, by virtue of specific mention, there is no eligibility for the transcendental potency in an ectypal sacrifice (vikṛti).
And in case of conflict, because of the distinctness of direct scriptural statement, the unexpressed [belongs] to the remainder.
Removal, however, is of a single part, because of connection with what already exists.
In the ectypal sacrifice, the remainder serves all purposes, as in the archetypal sacrifice.
Or it serves the primary purpose, because the subsidiary element is not enjoined [with respect to it].
[We reply:] No, because it is not within the context of the ritual topic, since the subsidiary element does not have that as its occasion.
Or [it is done] at that time, because of seeing an indicative textual mark.
The seeing of an indicative textual mark is [corroborative] in what is stated by reasoning.
Meat, however, [is the material] for the savanīya offerings, because there is no distinction in the injunction.
If it be said that secondary attribution is improper in the absence of proximity;
Now, therefore, [follows] the enquiry into what serves the sacrificial rite (kratvartha) and what serves the human purpose (puruṣārtha).
That in which there is pleasure for man [is puruṣārtha], because the desire to obtain it is not separated from its purpose.

sanskrit_iast: tadutsarge karmāṇi puruṣārthāya śāstrasyānatiśaṅkyatvān na ca dravyaṃ cikīrṣyate tenārthenābhisambandhāt kriyāyāṃ puruṣaśrutiḥ /
meaning: तदुत्सर्गे कर्माणि पुरुषार्थाय शास्त्रस्यानतिशङ्क्यत्वान् न च द्रव्यं चिकीर्ष्यते तेनार्थेनाभिसम्बन्धात् क्रियायां पुरुषश्रुतिः /
text_mt: Apart from that, the actions are for the human purpose because the sacred teaching is not to be called into question; nor is the substance intended to be produced; direct scriptural statement mentions man in connection with the action because of connection with that purpose.

sanskrit_iast: aviśeṣāt tu śāstrasya yathāśruti phalāni syuḥ /
meaning: अविशेषात् तु शास्त्रस्य यथाश्रुति फलानि स्युः /
text_mt: Because the sacred teaching is without distinction, the fruits should be according to direct scriptural statement.
Or rather, when no cause is grasped, [it is] for that purpose, because the purpose has no other connection.
Substances, however, would be given away without distinction, because of [otherwise] being useless.

sanskrit_iast: svena tvarthe na sambandho dravyāṇāṃ pṛthagarthatvāt tasmād yathāśruti syuḥ /
meaning: स्वेन त्वर्थे न सम्बन्धो द्रव्याणां पृथगर्थत्वात् तस्माद् यथाश्रुति स्युः /
text_mt: However, there is no connection [of the fruit] with its own purpose, because substances have distinct purposes; therefore they should be according to direct scriptural statement.
And they are enjoined in primary functional actions (arthakarma).
There, the oneness is not a subsidiary element of the sacrifice, because the object is subordinate.
[we reply:] it is not so, because there is no word expressing it, since that is the means of valid cognition, as in the prior case.

sanskrit_iast: śabdavat tūpalabhyate tadāgame hi taddṛśyate tasya jñānaṃ hi yathānyeṣām /
meaning: शब्दवत् तूपलभ्यते तदागमे हि तद्दृश्यते तस्य ज्ञानं हि यथान्येषाम् /
text_mt: Rather, it is apprehended like a word; for upon its arrival, it is perceived, because the cognition of it is just like that of other things.
And like that is the indicative textual mark seen.
In the substrates without distinction, the object would be apprehended as state of being.

sanskrit_iast: codanāyāṃ tv anārambho 'vibhaktatvān na hy anyena vidhīyate /
meaning: चोदनायां त्व् अनारम्भो ऽविभक्तत्वान् न ह्य् अन्येन विधीयते /
text_mt: In the injunctive rule, however, there is non-undertaking because it is undivided; for it is not enjoined by another.

sanskrit_iast: syād vā dravyacikīrṣāyāṃ bhāvo 'rthe ca guṇabhūtatāśrayād dhi guṇībhāvaḥ /
meaning: स्याद् वा द्रव्यचिकीर्षायां भावो ऽर्थे च गुणभूतताश्रयाद् धि गुणीभावः /
text_mt: Or rather, when there is a desire to produce the substance, there would be a state of being, and in the object, being subordinate; for subordination comes from resting on a substrate.
Therefore, with respect to the purpose, there is equality and inequality among offering substances and actions.
Because of a single accomplishment, all would be equal.
Or the curdled milk would be primary, because of the production of the blended essence.
And because of the commendation with the principal word.
The action on the footprint is not an impeller [of walking], because the leading [of the cow] serves another purpose.

sanskrit_iast: arthābhidhānakarma ca bhaviṣyatā saṃyogasya tannimittatvāt tadartho hi vidhīyate /
meaning: अर्थाभिधानकर्म च भविष्यता संयोगस्य तन्निमित्तत्वात् तदर्थो हि विधीयते /
text_mt: And the act of naming the object [is not an impeller], because the connection with what is yet to be is the cause of it; for it is enjoined for its sake.
In the animal sacrifice, blood and dung have no ritual action, because of the absence of touching.
And the substance of a single part [serves], because of its connection with what is spoken in the originative injunction.
If it is argued that from the specific designation it is other than the [primary] object,
In the sprinkling of clarified butter, because of remoteness, there would be a separate vessel, as in the case of the after-offerings.

sanskrit_iast: na vā pātratvād apātratvaṃ tv ekadeśatvāt /
meaning: न वा पात्रत्वाद् अपात्रत्वं त्व् एकदेशत्वात् /
text_mt: Or rather, not so, because of its being a vessel; whereas non-vesselhood would be because of its being a part.
And because there is a reason for joint application.
The bringing together, however, would be the principal, on account of an indicative textual mark being seen.
For in the presence of an explicit statement, there is incapacity of the explanatory reason.
There, the originative production would be undivided.
There, that belonging to the juhū spoon is for the purpose of prohibiting the after-offerings.
If it is argued that that belonging to the upabhṛt spoon is likewise,
[we say:] it would be an obligatory restatement because of the prohibition regarding the juhū spoon.
That has the number eight, because of direct hearing.
And because of the benefit to that belonging to the juhū spoon.

sanskrit_iast: dvayos tu hetusāmarthayaṃ śravaṇaṃ ca samānayane /
meaning: द्वयोस् तु हेतुसामर्थयं श्रवणं च समानयने /
text_mt: In the case of both, however, there is efficacy of the reason and direct hearing in the bringing together.
The sacrificial chip, however, is accomplished from another source, because the word designates its own action.
And one suspects it because of a difference in species.
Or rather, it is a single part of that [sacrificial post], because that is the cause of its state as a chip.
And because of its being seen for each sacrificial post.
In the case of the branch, because it is the principal.

sanskrit_iast: śākhāyāṃ tatpradhānatvād upaveṣeṇa vibhāgaḥ syād vaiṣamyaṃ tat /
meaning: शाखायां तत्प्रधानत्वाद् उपवेषेण विभागः स्याद् वैषम्यं तत् /
text_mt: In the case of the branch, because it is the principal, there would be division with the fire-stick; that would be inequality.

sanskrit_iast: haraṇe tu juhotir yogasāmānyād dravyāṇāṃ cārthaśeṣatvāt /
meaning: हरणे तु जुहोतिर् योगसामान्याद् द्रव्याणां चार्थशेषत्वात् /
text_mt: In the conveying, however, the root 'juhu' is used because of the commonality of connection, and because substances are subsidiary to the purpose.
Or it is a disposal rite, because the word makes that primary.
[we say:] no, because of non-eligibility for it, and because the purpose has already been accomplished.
Because there is no connection in origin, there would be a division of the consecrated waters, like clarified butter.
Or rather, the disposal rite is of those meant for kneading, and of the others, because that is the primary element.
The handing over of the staff to the Maitrāvaruṇa priest is like the casting away, because its purpose has been accomplished.
Or it is a primary functional action, like the garland, because of its connection with an agent.
And because it is seen in connection with a ritual action.

sanskrit_iast: utpattau yena saṃyuktaṃ tadarthaṃ tacchrutihetutvāt tasyārthāntaragamane śeṣatvāt pratipattiḥ syāt /
meaning: उत्पत्तौ येन संयुक्तं तदर्थं तच्छ्रुतिहेतुत्वात् तस्यार्थान्तरगमने शेषत्वात् प्रतिपत्तिः स्यात् /
text_mt: That with which a thing is connected in origin is for the sake of that, because it is the cause of that direct scriptural statement; upon its moving to another purpose, it would be a disposal rite because of being a remainder.
And in the soma sacrifice, because its purpose has been fulfilled.
Or it is a primary functional action, because of its connection with naming.
Or it is a disposal rite, because of conforming to that principle; the direct scriptural statement regarding the Avabhṛtha is for the purpose of [specifying] the place.
There is no injunction of agent, place, and time, because of their constant coexistence in the performance.
Similarly, the direct scriptural statement of a subordinate quality in substances is due to connection with the originative [injunction].
And in the case of a preparatory purification, because that is primary.
The injunction 'yajati' constitutes an action with substance and deity, because of being accomplished in the aggregate.
Because it is heard when that is stated, 'juhoti' must denote something additional: pouring in.
Because an injunctive rule terminates with the action, an extension of the injunctive rule would apply to another object.

meaning: अपि वोत्पत्तिसंयोगाद् अर्थसम्बन्धो ऽविशिष्टानां प्रयोगैकत्वहेतुः स्यात् /
text_mt: Rather, because of connection with originative [injunction], the connection with an object among undistinguished [actions] would be the cause of unity of performance.
In actions of preparatory purification of substances, because they are for the sake of another, the direct statement of a fruit must be a corroborative statement.
And because originative [injunction] is not predominantly for that.
The fruit, however, belongs to that which is predominantly for it.
In an occasional rite, because it is a modification, another [act] would be the primary element of the sacrifice.
When one [act] possesses both [characters], however, there is distinctness of connection.
The preparatory purification of substances meant for actions, however, would be a duty serving the sacrificial rite.
Because of distinctness, it must be distributed.

sanskrit_iast: codanāyāṃ phalāśruteḥ karmamātraṃ vidhīyeta na hy aśabdaṃ pratīyate /
meaning: चोदनायां फलाश्रुतेः कर्ममात्रं विधीयेत न ह्य् अशब्दं प्रतीयते /
text_mt: Since no fruit is heard in the injunction, merely an action would be enjoined; for what is not expressed by word cannot be apprehended.

sanskrit_iast: api vāmnānasāmatharthyāc codanārthena gamyetārthānāṃ hy arthatvena vacanāni pratīyante 'rthatopy asamarthānām ānantarye 'py asambandhas tasmāc chrutyekadeśaḥ saḥ /
meaning: अपि वाम्नानसामथर्थ्याच् चोदनार्थेन गम्येतार्थानां ह्य् अर्थत्वेन वचनानि प्रतीयन्ते ऽर्थतोप्य् असमर्थानाम् आनन्तर्ये ऽप्य् असम्बन्धस् तस्माच् छ्रुत्येकदेशः सः /
text_mt: Rather, through the efficacy of the sacred text, it is apprehended through the purpose of the injunction; for Vedic statements are understood as having meaning by virtue of having a beneficial purpose; even if contiguous, there is no syntactical connection for words lacking semantic capacity; therefore, it is part of the direct scriptural statement.
And the meaning of the sentence is like that which has a secondary quality as its object.
It serves all purposes, because of non-specification.
That [fruit] must be heaven, because it is non-distinct in relation to all persons.
In a sacrificial rite, the fruit is a corroborative statement, like [that of] a subsidiary element, so holds Kārṣṇājini.

sanskrit_iast: phalamātreyo nirdeśād aśrutau hy anumānaṃ syāt /
meaning: फलमात्रेयो निर्देशाद् अश्रुतौ ह्य् अनुमानं स्यात् /
text_mt: It is the fruit, Ātreya holds, because of explicit mention; for in the absence of a direct scriptural statement, there would be inference.
With regard to subsidiary elements, it is a eulogy, because of being for the sake of another.

sanskrit_iast: kāmye karmaṇi nityaḥ svarge yathā yajñāṅge kratvarthaḥ /
meaning: काम्ये कर्मणि नित्यः स्वर्गे यथा यज्ञाङ्गे क्रत्वर्थः /
text_mt: In an optional action, it is obligatory with respect to heaven, as in the case of a subsidiary element of the sacrifice serving the sacrificial rite.
Or rather, desire is enjoined in connection with it.
And when it has disappeared, the restrictive injunction is for the purpose thereof.
All desire-motivated [rites belong to it], by means of the desires for subsidiary elements, because of the context of the ritual topic.
Or it is an instruction of the fruit, because of connection with the word denoting the primary element.
Or it is the accomplishment of the etymological sense, because the object is not connected with the originative [injunction].
In coexistence, the connection with the injunction is meaningful.
If it is objected that when time is directly stated in scripture, it is time [that is enjoined],
It would not be so because of non-inherence with the purpose.

sanskrit_iast: anutpattau tu kālaḥ syāt prayojanena sambandhāt /
meaning: अनुत्पत्तौ तु कालः स्यात् प्रयोजनेन सम्बन्धात् /
text_mt: Where there is no originative [injunction], however, it would be time, because of connection with the purpose.
In the scope of the time of origin, it would be the time, because the sentence has that as its principal element.

sanskrit_iast: phalasaṃyogas tv acodite na syād aśeṣabhūtatvāt /
meaning: फलसंयोगस् त्व् अचोदिते न स्याद् अशेषभूतत्वात् /
text_mt: The connection with a fruit, however, would not occur when unenjoined, because of not being an accessory.
The connection with interruption in the case of subsidiary elements, however, is for the purpose of a motivating condition.
Because of connection with the primary element, the subsidiary elements share the time of the primary element.

sanskrit_iast: apavṛtte tu codanā tatsāmānyāt svakāle syāt /
meaning: अपवृत्ते तु चोदना तत्सामान्यात् स्वकाले स्यात् /
text_mt: When it has ceased, however, the injunction would apply at its own time, because of its commonality with that.
Rather, the non-sacrifices would be subsidiary elements, because of being distinct from that.
That which stands in the middle belongs to the middle of that.

sanskrit_iast: sarvāsāṃ vā samatvāc codanātaḥ syān na hi tasya prakaraṇaṃ deśārtham ucyate madhye /
meaning: सर्वासां वा समत्वाच् चोदनातः स्यान् न हि तस्य प्रकरणं देशार्थम् उच्यते मध्ये /
text_mt: Or it belongs to all because of equality by virtue of the injunction; for its context of the ritual topic is not stated for the purpose of place in the middle.
And when there is no distinction in the context of the ritual topic, both are indeed mutually contradictory.

sanskrit_iast: api vā kālamātraṃ syād adarśanād viśeśasya /
meaning: अपि वा कालमात्रं स्याद् अदर्शनाद् विशेशस्य /
text_mt: Rather, it would be mere time, because no distinction is observed.
Or that which has a fruit would be the primary element for the other, on account of the stated reason.
The curd cup is occasional, because of connection with a direct scriptural statement.
And it is obligatory, because of the word 'senior'.

sanskrit_iast: nityo vā syād arthavādastayoḥ karmaṇy asambandhād bhaṅgitvāc cāntarāyasya /
meaning: नित्यो वा स्याद् अर्थवादस्तयोः कर्मण्य् असम्बन्धाद् भङ्गित्वाच् चान्तरायस्य /
text_mt: Or it may be obligatory, because an explanatory praise has no connection to their action and because the interruption has lapsed.

sanskrit_iast: vaiśvānaraś ca nityaḥ syān nityaiḥ samānasaṅkhyatvāt /
meaning: वैश्वानरश् च नित्यः स्यान् नित्यैः समानसङ्ख्यत्वात् /
text_mt: And the Vaiśvānara [sacrifice] must be obligatory, because it has an equal enumeration with obligatory rites.
Or [it is optional], on the view of its connection with what has already originated.
There is a sixfold layer, because it has preceding [layers].
And because it has an equal enumeration with them.

sanskrit_iast: ekacitir vā syād apavṛkte hi codyate nimittena /
meaning: एकचितिर् वा स्याद् अपवृक्ते हि चोद्यते निमित्तेन /
text_mt: Or there should be a single layer; for it is enjoined by an occasion upon completion.
The equal enumeration with them is due to contradiction.
The ancestral sacrifice (pitṛyajña), having its own time, cannot be a subsidiary element.
And because it is enumerated equally [as an independent rite].
And because it is observed even when [the main rite is] prohibited.
The rope would be a subsidiary element of the sacrificial animal, because it is enjoined upon its arrival.
Or it is a subsidiary element of the sacrificial post (yūpa), because of consecrating it.
And the explanatory praise has that purpose.
And the chip of wood (svaru) as well, because it is a part [of the post].
And the redemption, just like its subsidiary element.
Or rather, it is a subsidiary element of the animal, because it is a primary functional action.
The statement of redemption must be figurative.
In the New- and Full-Moon sacrifices, the offerings are primary elements, without distinction.

sanskrit_iast: api vāṅgāni kāni cidyeśvaṅgatvena saṃstutiḥ sāmānyo hy abhisaṃstavaḥ /
meaning: अपि वाङ्गानि कानि चिद्येश्वङ्गत्वेन संस्तुतिः सामान्यो ह्य् अभिसंस्तवः /
text_mt: Or some are subsidiary elements, where there is praise in the capacity of a subsidiary; for commendation is general.
And likewise there is indication of another purpose.

sanskrit_iast: avaśiṣṭaṃ tu kāraṇaṃ pradhāneṣu guṇasya vidyamānatvāt /
meaning: अवशिष्टं तु कारणं प्रधानेषु गुणस्य विद्यमानत्वात् /
text_mt: The remaining factor, however, is that it is among the primary elements, because the subordinate quality is present.
An indication of another purpose is not found where it is not stated, because it serves another.

sanskrit_iast: pṛthavatve tv abhidhānayor niveśaḥ śrutito vyapadeśāc ca tatpunarmukhyalakṣaṇaṃ yatphalavatvaṃ tatsannidhāv asaṃyuktaṃ tadaṅgaṃsyādbhāgitvāt kāraṇasyāśrutaś cānyasambandhaḥ /
meaning: पृथवत्वे त्व् अभिधानयोर् निवेशः श्रुतितो व्यपदेशाच् च तत्पुनर्मुख्यलक्षणं यत्फलवत्वं तत्सन्निधाव् असंयुक्तं तदङ्गंस्याद्भागित्वात् कारणस्याश्रुतश् चान्यसम्बन्धः /
text_mt: When there is separateness, however, the application of both designations follows from direct scriptural statement and mention; but the characteristic of the principal rite is that which possesses a result; what is not connected in proximity to that would be its subsidiary element, because it partakes of the cause, and no other connection is heard.
And secondary qualities connected with a name are enjoined; they do not apply to subsidiary elements.
And the direct scriptural statement of the cause is equal; the relation of subsidiary and principal is with others.
The connection is at the origination; therefore, it must be the teaching of a subsidiary element.
And likewise there is indication of another purpose.
In the Jyotiṣṭoma, they are equal; for the cause is without distinction.

sanskrit_iast: guṇānāṃ tūtpattivākyena sambandhāt kāraṇaśrutis tasmāt somaḥ pradhānaṃ syāt /
meaning: गुणानां तूत्पत्तिवाक्येन सम्बन्धात् कारणश्रुतिस् तस्मात् सोमः प्रधानं स्यात् /
